clue.text: Cleric accommodates lawyer and editor

indicators.note: the cleric takes in, or houses, the lawyer, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A churchman gives lodging to a solicitor and a newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: A redactor prepares text for publication, which is the work of an editor.

clue.text: Go and change partners

explanation.surface: Advice to dancers or couples: get going and swap who you are with.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair to a place is to go there; read as re-pair, it means to pair up again with someone new.

clue.text: Give lecturer a teaset

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Give lecturer a teaset (6)': DON (lecturer) is clear but 'a teaset' does not give ATE; the clue looks garbled in OCR and no source gives the printed text

clue.text: About to slow down and stop

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
to ease is to slacken or slow down

explanation.surface: An instruction to reduce speed and halt.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease is to come to a halt or stop doing something.

clue.text: Private lists delivered by Joan of Arc

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers such as privates who are not officers
a ship that lists leans to one side

explanation.surface: Inventories handed out personally by the French saint.
explanation.walkthrough: Joan of Arc relieved the siege of the French city in 1429, earning the title 'the Maid of' that city; 'delivered' means freed, not handed over.
explanation.definitionFit: The French city Joan of Arc liberated from English siege in 1429.

clue.text: Displayed by egghead of portly frame

indicators.note: the portly word forms a frame around the egg's head, so it surrounds the other piece

parts.note: portly means stout, plump
the head of the word egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: Something shown off by a tubby intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual, but it gives only the first letter of egg, which sits inside STOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Things set out are arranged on show, that is, displayed.

clue.text: To go into detail is complicated

explanation.surface: Saying that expanding on something makes it intricate.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to expand on a point at length; as an adjective it means intricate, involved.

clue.text: Totally apt as a Socialist electioneering slogan

definitions.text: apt as a Socialist electioneering slogan

explanation.surface: A slogan described as entirely suitable for a left-wing campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it in two: a left-wing party would campaign for its opponents on the right to be out.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means completely; read as 'Out, Right!' it is a call to vote the right-wing party out.

clue.text: Margery let up when wire was delivered

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the words are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: taken as written, a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman relaxed once a cable arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading MARGELET backwards from 'up' gives the letters; 'wire' is the old word for a telegram, not a metal strand.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire is an informal term for a telegram sent by telegraph.

clue.text: Tiptop trainee in a small boat

indicators.note: the trainee is placed in the boat, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a pinnace is a small boat carried by a larger ship
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: An excellent apprentice sitting in a dinghy.
explanation.definitionFit: The pinnacle is the very top, the highest point.

clue.text: Glue left on a Degas picture, maybe

parts.note: paste is a glue

explanation.surface: Adhesive left on a painting by the French artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Degas worked often in coloured chalk sticks, so many of his works are examples of this medium.

clue.text: Accustomed to being manipulated

explanation.surface: Someone who has got used to being exploited.
explanation.definitionFit: To be used to something is to be accustomed to it; someone used is exploited or manipulated.

clue.text: Where Catholics take communion collectively

explanation.surface: Describing where and how Catholics receive the sacrament together.
explanation.definitionFit: Communion is received during the Mass; 'in the mass' also means as a whole, taken collectively.

clue.text: Due appeal to air-force unit

parts.note: O is the exclamation of appeal or invocation, as in 'O Lord'
a wing is a formation in an air force

explanation.surface: A deserved plea made to an RAF formation.
explanation.definitionFit: Owing means outstanding, still to be paid, as a debt is due.

clue.text: Is on the fiddle, despite respectful greetings

explanation.surface: Someone cheating while being outwardly polite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the fiddle' is British slang for cheating; here it means literally playing a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: A violinist draws the bow across the strings; bending the body in greeting is also called this.

clue.text: Finished sketch gains credit

parts.note: over means ended, finished
a draft is a rough sketch or outline

explanation.surface: A completed drawing earns praise.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank allowing an account into the red is extending credit to the customer.

clue.text: Play about the church makes money in Athens

indicators.note: the play goes round the church, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a drama is a play
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A theatre piece about the church earns money in Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek unit of currency used before the euro.

clue.text: Money talks, Dad, and it's sweet

indicators.note: talks says the word for money is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money
pop is an informal name for a father

explanation.surface: Cash speaks, father, and that is lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money talks' looks like the proverb, but 'talks' signals the sound of LOLLY, slang for cash in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled sweet on a stick is a classic example of this confection.

clue.text: Refuse to give in project

explanation.surface: Advice to hold firm on a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold out stubbornly is to stick it out; something that juts or projects sticks out.

clue.text: He got no break at work

indicators.note: break suggests the words are smashed apart and their letters rebuilt

explanation.surface: A worker complains of getting no rest on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' reads as a rest from work but is the anagram signal for HEGOTNO.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone busy and active is said to be constantly moving, working.

clue.text: Old chum is a gem

parts.note: a pal is a chum, a friend

explanation.surface: An elderly friend is described as a treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A milky iridescent stone prized as a precious jewel.

clue.text: Cad is trodden underfoot

explanation.surface: A scoundrel gets walked all over.
explanation.definitionFit: A heel is a contemptible man; the back of the foot or shoe is what is trodden down in walking.

clue.text: Chief male publicity agent

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
an adman works in advertising and publicity

explanation.surface: A senior man who runs advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: A headman is the leader of a village or tribe, its chief.

clue.text: Cryptographers do fish in a Scottish river

indicators.note: the fish swims in the river, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Dee flows through Aberdeenshire in Scotland
the cod is a fish

explanation.surface: Code-breakers fish in a Highland river.
explanation.definitionFit: Code-breakers work out the plain meaning of a coded message.

clue.text: Coming before Christmas

explanation.surface: Something arriving ahead of the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: An advent is an arrival; with a capital it is the church season leading up to the Nativity.

clue.text: Peer receives master with added spirit

indicators.note: the peer takes in the master, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: LD is the abbreviation for Lord, a peer
an ace is an expert, a master of a skill

explanation.surface: A nobleman welcomes an expert who brings extra vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with added spirit' means a drink with alcohol slipped in, not liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffee laced has had brandy or whisky poured in.

clue.text: A role he and I had in segregation

parts.note: a part is a role in a play
taken as written
taken as written
D is the contraction of had, as in I'd

explanation.surface: Two actors share a part in a drama about racial division.
explanation.definitionFit: The former South African policy of racial separation.

clue.text: Dance with energy? Nonsense!

parts.note: to trip is to dance lightly, as in 'trip the light fantastic'
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of dancing energetically.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is offal, and figuratively worthless rubbish talk.

clue.text: Vocal viscount's son embraced by friend

indicators.note: the friend hugs the son, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a viscount's son is styled the Honourable, abbreviated Hon

explanation.surface: An outspoken aristocrat's boy hugged by a mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonal means relating to the voice or speech sounds.

clue.text: His appetite is all-consuming!

parts.note: all-consuming reads as obsessive, but literally means eating everything, both plants and meat

explanation.surface: A man with a voracious, obsessive hunger.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that eats both plant and animal food will eat anything.

clue.text: Little sweetheart, I take note

parts.note: pet is a term of endearment, like sweetheart
taken as written
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A small darling says she will take a note.
explanation.definitionFit: Petite describes someone small and dainty in build.
